evidence: AdvanceOrderUseCase, CancelOrderUseCase, PlaceOrderUseCase and ListOrdersByStatusUseCase only reach persistence through the injected `orders: OrderRepository` (findById, save, findByStatus)
GetStockLevelsUseCase reaches persistence only through `products: ProductRepository.findAll()`
dto.ts defines `toOrderDto` and `toStockLevelDto` once, and every use case calls them
ListOrdersByStatusUseCase delegates validation to the domain's `assertOrderStatus(status)` instead of writing its own check
AdvanceOrderUseCase.execute and CancelOrderUseCase.execute both contain `if (!order) throw new DomainError("not_found", ...)`. This is a minor repeated lookup guard, not a duplicated domain rule
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The src/application module covers one concern: the order and stock use cases plus the DTO mapping they share. Every use case takes the domain ports through its constructor (OrderRepository, ProductRepository, StockReservationService, IdGenerator). None of them uses a database, ORM or query client directly. The DTO mapping is defined once in dto.ts as toOrderDto and toStockLevelDto, and every use case calls those functions rather than building DTOs by hand. Status validation is delegated to the domain's assertOrderStatus. AdvanceOrderUseCase and CancelOrderUseCase both repeat the same one-line not-found guard after findById. I treated that as a trivial lookup guard, not a business rule or invariant written out twice, so it does not count as a violation. A stricter reading would flag it. The customerId check in PlaceOrderUseCase might also repeat validation in the Order constructor, but the domain source isn't provided, so I couldn't confirm that.
